indicators.note: follows tells us the word for quickly comes after the word for interval

parts.note: an interval is a break, as between halves or lessons
fast means quickly, as in running fast

explanation.surface: Someone eats a meal in a short interval, bolting it down fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The first meal of the day is one specific kind of meal.

clue.text: Batterer featured on newssheet causes storm

indicators.note: featured on means placed on top of, which in a down entry puts the batterer above the sheet

parts.note: a ram batters, whether a battering ram or a butting sheep
a page is one sheet of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A violent attacker appears in the newspaper and causes an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm about is to charge around wildly and angrily, the verb sense of running amok.

parts.note: the letters of the first word rearranged spell the third word, so one stands for the other as an example of a word-shuffle

explanation.surface: Someone longed for a dean's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yearned for' reads as longing, but 'for' means 'standing in place of': YEARNED and DEANERY share the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made by rearranging another word's letters is the device described; yearned and deanery are such a pair.

clue.text: Speed, might one say, to castle

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as ..., the quality of being quick, hence 'might one say'
a stronghold or secure fortified place

explanation.surface: Someone races off to a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might one say' flags that the speed sense is a playful coinage: fast plus -ness.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress or remote stronghold is called this, and the word could also jokingly mean quickness.

parts.note: toff is British slang for an upper-class person or aristocrat

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters of expensive

explanation.surface: A posh person buys a very costly confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter is a classic sweet.

clue.text: Driver may take dazzling risk with it

definitions.text: Driver may take dazzling risk with it

parts.words: Driver may take dazzling risk with it
parts.note: a motorist who leaves the main beam on risks dazzling oncoming traffic with the lamp at the front of the car

explanation.surface: A motorist takes a spectacular gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dazzling risk' sounds like a bold gamble, but it is the literal risk of blinding other drivers with a car lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The front lamp of a car can blind oncoming motorists if left on full beam.

clue.text: Improved and kept ball repeatedly in play

definitions.meaning: recovered or got better, as a market or a patient does
in tennis, players hit the ball back and forth in a long exchange

explanation.surface: A tennis player got better and kept long exchanges going.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering strength and exchanging long series of shots in tennis share one verb.

parts.note: reads like a check on a car's essential fluid levels, but the vital fluid is the one in our veins and the check a medical one

explanation.surface: A mechanic checks the essential oil and water levels.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen tempts you towards car maintenance; the vital fluid is the one the body cannot live without.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical sample of a patient's circulating fluid analysed for levels of sugar, iron and so on.

definitions.meaning: main or principal, as in the main winner of a race
a protective coat or one-piece work suit

explanation.surface: What does the boss wear?
explanation.definitionFit: The principal winner is the 'overall' winner, and a workman's protective coat bears the same name.

clue.text: No progress here I'm out of date

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
passé, borrowed from French, means old-fashioned or out of date

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being stuck and behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a situation where no forward movement is possible.

clue.text: I foiled new production of opera

indicators.note: a new production restages the material, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of thwarting a fresh staging of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new production of' turns I FOILED into the opera's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's only work for the operatic stage bears this title.

definitions.meaning: financial support from a backer, as of the arts
the steady trade a shop receives from its loyal customers

explanation.surface: Being sponsored is a matter of habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing from a benefactor and the steady business of loyal customers are both called this.

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word get

parts.note: roused means stirred up or excited

explanation.surface: Someone moaned, starting to get worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble or whinge is to complain, and this is the colloquial past tense.

clue.text: What the colonel is charged with?

definitions.text: What the colonel is charged with?

parts.words: What the colonel is charged with?
parts.note: sounds like an accusation in court, but it is the body of soldiers placed in the colonel's charge

explanation.surface: What crime has the colonel been accused of?
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged with' suggests a criminal charge; here it means entrusted with command of a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel traditionally commands a military unit of several battalions.

clue.text: Herald, messenger-he was a bit of each

definitions.text: Herald, messenger-he was a bit of each

indicators.note: a bit of means only the opening part of the word Herald is used
each extends the same treatment to the word messenger, so only its opening part is used too

explanation.surface: A Greek god served both as herald and messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three letters of Herald and of messenger join up; the whole clue also describes the Greek god who carried the gods' messages.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the son of Zeus served as herald and courier to the Olympians.

clue.text: Pleasant sounds: spoil with horrid noise

parts.note: to harm something is to spoil or damage it

indicators.note: horrid suggests the word noise is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lovely music is ruined by an ugly racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link, and 'horrid noise' reads as the opposite of the definition, which is what makes the surface work.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes sounding agreeably together make musical concords.

parts.note: reads like innocent youthful charm, but the sweetness is a chocolate treat given to children at an April festival

explanation.surface: Springtime has a special sweetness for the young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetness' is literal: a chocolate confection, and 'spring' points to the Christian festival held in that season.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate treat in an oval shape is traditionally given to children at the spring festival.

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the word for resign
failed suggests the word has has gone wrong, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to quit is to resign from a job

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister has failed and is about to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'nearly', but it is the container signal; H.H. Asquith was British Liberal Prime Minister 1908-16.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Henry Asquith was Liberal Prime Minister of Britain before Lloyd George.

indicators.note: poor suggests a bad performance, so the letters of the climber's word are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A struggling mountaineer takes a fall he cannot control.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning nosedive by an aircraft, figuratively any out-of-control decline.

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet
re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a sage is a wise expert or pundit

explanation.surface: An expert issues a subdued prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell or portend something is to predict it.

definitions.meaning: split into two words, the entry describes being present at an England international cricket match, a Test
to affirm formally or bear witness

explanation.surface: Cricket fans watch the England side declare their innings.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; 'declare' looks like a cricket term (ending an innings) but is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm or bear witness that something is true is to state it formally.

definitions.meaning: to tat is to make lace by knotting thread, so people who do it

explanation.surface: Lace-makers dressed in torn clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace-knotters and torn scraps of cloth share one spelling.

parts.note: to scour is to scrub hard

indicators.note: almost means the word get is used without its final letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for washing up, then fetching the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, and a whip used for punishment is a lash.

clue.text: Keep going over same ground in army training

definitions.text: Keep going over same ground in army training

parts.words: Keep going over same ground in army training
parts.note: in drill, soldiers march on the spot, lifting their feet without moving forward

explanation.surface: Recruits repeatedly cover the same ground in drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep going over same ground' hints at repetition, but it is literally marching in place; figuratively, it means waiting without progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching on the spot in drill, and by extension waiting idly, is this military phrase.

indicators.note: confined by means the boy is placed inside the month

parts.note: May is a month of the year
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is laid up for a month by sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease or ailment is an illness.

clue.text: Laid out an extraordinary form of worship

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests something out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual kind of devotion is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid out' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder with 'an'; 'extraordinary' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive admiration or flattery is a kind of hero-worship.

clue.text: A breather here under the bridge

definitions.text: A breather here under the bridge

parts.words: A breather here under the bridge
parts.note: the bridge is that of the nose, and below it are the openings we breathe through

explanation.surface: Someone takes a rest beneath a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' suggests a rest and 'bridge' a river crossing; both are about the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two openings below the nasal bridge lets air in and out.

clue.text: Seems a political aide catches attention

indicators.note: catches means the aide's letters hold the word for attention inside them

parts.note: PPS is a Parliamentary Private Secretary, a British MP who assists a minister
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A minister's assistant seems to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To look or give the impression of being something is to seem.

definitions.meaning: reserved or occupied, like a hired taxi or busy phone line
entered into combat with an enemy

explanation.surface: A fighter is booked for a bout and joins battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserved and having entered combat with the enemy share one word.

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of urges Tony are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teenager presses Tony to mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person, such as an adolescent, is a teen.
